OpenAI sparked Hugging Face bids with early investment offer ahead of Nvidia's $13 billion deal
Nvidia releases software platform to stop AI agents from misbehaving
SpaceX launches its massive Starship rocket into orbit for the first time
Earlier this month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei rocked the tech sector by urging AI companies to slow how quickly they improve their most advanced models and calling for stronger government oversight. He published a three-step proposal aimed at tempering the pace of development without "sacrificing commercial advantage or the United States' lead in AI."
Several of Amodei's competitors, including OpenAI CEO
Sam Altman
and SpaceX CEO
Elon Musk
, expressed support for his proposal, while others, including
Meta
CEO
Mark Zuckerberg
and
Nvidia
CEO Jensen Huang, argued that individual companies should be responsible for ensuring the safety of their products.
President
Donald Trump
convened top executives from
Alphabet
,
Meta
,
SpaceX
, Nvidia,
Palantir
, Anthropic, OpenAI and other companies on Tuesday to discuss the issue. The group signed a short voluntary, nonbinding accord, which says that "every company is responsible for developing its own technology safely and in a way that builds trust with customers and the public."
"We all need to work together to make sure that we can win, and we can win safely," Amodei said outside the White House on Tuesday. "If we do this right, if we work with the president and everyone here, we can win safely."

data.title: Book of Shapes – Collection of minimal, generative and customizable SVG-patterns
data.author: eustoria
data.article_summary: 《Book of Shapes》是Nikolaj Sokolowski创作的SVG图案合集，专注于极简、生成式和可自定义设计。作品按网格、径向、噪声、流动、等距、有机、畸变和物理等类别分类，包含Flow Dots、Triangular Mosaic、Spiral Morph、Iso Sphere等众多图案，并提供“最新、热门、喜欢”等浏览方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个生成式视觉艺术/图形设计项目的审美价值、创作方式、应用场景及原创性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **审美认可**：评论者认为作品“漂亮”，联想到 Adam Fuhrer 的视觉艺术；也有人称赞其作品集合，说明整体视觉效果获得肯定。  
• **相似项目与技术实践**：有人正在开发类似工具，主要用 Python 脚本生成可在浏览器中重新着色的 SVG 壁纸，并提到 Claude 配合脚手架能高效生成此类脚本。  
• **实用设计价值**：有人希望将这类生成式图案用于制作更具特色的演示文稿，尤其是 PowerPoint 默认形状之外的圆角六边形、squircle、飘带和 blob 等形状。  
• **使用场景存疑**：有评论者不理解目标用户是谁，以及该项目具体适合如何、在哪里使用，反映出产品定位和应用说明可能不够清晰。  
• **原创性争议**：有人质疑内容是否“照搬” Turtletoy，争议焦点在于作品与既有平台内容的相似程度及其来源、署名问题。  

补充讨论：另有评论指出界面细节问题——“Liked”按钮没有显示图形；总体上，讨论以正面评价为主，同时关注工具用途、灵感来源和交互完善度。

data.title: Context Language Models
data.author: emersonmacro
data.article_summary: 论文提出“上下文语言模型”（CLM）：将上下文视为可由模型自由读写的文件，使模型自主管理重要信息，并支持多智能体共享或并存上下文。实验显示，CLM在浏览、长时任务和多仓库协作中，以更少计算获得更高性能；还支持自然语言技能优化和在线强化学习。论文进一步提出后缀缓存复用，将服务端计算开销降低35%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“上下文管理模型（CLM）”如何维护、更新和优化LLM上下文，以及缓存失效、计算成本和系统架构展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **独立管理器更优**：bob1029认为让主智能体自行管理记忆会占用有限的注意力和token，最好由独立的“超管智能体”按不同调度管理上下文，从而降低主任务负担并更好控制缓存失效。  
• **方法并非全新**：visarga指出，普通模型也可以把文件作为下一轮上下文传入，只是修改会带来缓存重算成本；CLM的优势可能在于减少或忽略这类重算。  
• **技术价值在缓存机制**：svachalek认为上下文管理是当前LLM的重要痛点，缓存失效（cache busting）是关键难题；Bolwin进一步指出，论文可能最重要的发现是保留无效缓存后缀也未明显损害性能。  
• **未来系统化发展**：vatsachak预测CLM会与主模型联合训练，并形成类似数据库“冷热页面”的多层上下文管理，甚至出现“Context as a DB”方向。  
• **系统抽象类比**：plastic-enjoyer将“上下文作为文件”类比为LLM的RAM，并追问是否需要重新设计类似MMU的内存管理抽象。  
• **扩展性与趋势判断**：有人将其视为“Bitter Lesson”在上下文管理上的再次体现；另有评论提供“Recursive Language Models”作为相关工作。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是CLM究竟是实质性的新架构，还是对现有“文件追加上下文”方法的优化；核心权衡在于管理开销、缓存命中率与上下文质量。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), language models that natively manage their own context. We implement this by treating the context as a file and allowing the model to make unrestricted updates to this file. This allows the model to learn what is most important to maintain in context, and naturally extends to multi-agent systems where multiple agent contexts coexist as files. Building CLMs zero-shot with existing models outperforms SOTA context management strategies across a variety of tasks: 11.4% higher accuracy with 21.5% fewer FLOPs on BrowseComp-Plus, 5% higher scores with 59% fewer FLOPs on 12-hour EdgeBench, and 65% greater improvement with the same compute on a 24-hour multi-repository agent-swarm task. Moreover, by shifting context management from external harness control to intrinsic model behavior, CLMs naturally enable both in-context and parametric learning of context-management strategies. We show that CLMs can be steered with natural-language instructions evolved through a standard skill-optimization loop, improving held-out accuracy by up to 35.9 points on a context-management task while reducing compute. We also introduce an online reinforcement learning method for CLMs, improving Qwen3.5-9B performance on BrowseComp-Plus by 47.6% while using 12% fewer FLOPs. Finally, we co-design Suffix Cache Reuse for CLM serving, further reducing server-side compute by 35% relative to standard SGLang at matched performance.

data.title: Adding Floating-Point Decimals for Fun and Profit
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 文章解释了十进制小数在双精度浮点数中的表示与运算误差。以“0.1+0.2≠0.3”为例，介绍浮点数结构、ulp、输入与加法舍入，以及结果转为十进制显示的规则。文章进一步探讨为何金额相加时误差常不明显，并分析误差呈现特定图案的原因。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：货币及小数计算中，浮点数、整数、Decimal 等表示方式的精确性、舍入问题，以及存储与展示的设计取舍。

不同观点：
• **整数（以分存储）更稳妥**：将金额按“分”转换为整数进行计算和存储，展示时再转为元/分，可避免二进制浮点误差。但若未来要求显示三位或更多小数，就可能需要调整存储逻辑。  
• **使用 Decimal 更具扩展性**：评论认为金额精度需求可能变化，因此直接使用十进制定点数比固定存储“分”更安全；不过在格式完全由自己控制的纯文本账本中，整数方案仍更方便。  
• **64 位浮点数未必实际有问题**：有人反驳“货币不能用浮点数”的常见说法，认为对现实金额而言，JavaScript 等使用的 64 位浮点数精度足以在最终结果四舍五入到分时满足需求。  
• **任何表示方式都无法消除业务舍入**：例如年费100美元，按月分摊时每月账单只能保留到分，全年相加可能少于100美元。争议焦点因此不仅是数据类型精度，也包括计费周期和舍入规则。

补充讨论：有人提到 Python 的分数类型及可构造实数，可支持更高或任意精度；另有评论仅指出页面图片先于文字加载、视觉上像1像素网格，属于界面体验问题，与核心技术讨论关系较弱。

49893519.article_content:
Many people know that you shouldn’t do decimal calculations, such as
those involving U.S. dollars and cents, with the floating-point numbers
in most programming languages. This is because decimal numbers can’t be
expressed exactly as such floating-point numbers, so you will encounter
rounding errors.
Famously, with
IEEE
double-precision floats
,
0.1 + 0.2
is not
0.3
, but rather,
0.30000000000000004
.
On the other hand, I use a Python REPL to add up decimal numbers for
receipts all the time. Of course, my stakes are lower; I’m summing
things in the $1–$100 range and know to manually round the microscopic
errors off before copying the sum somewhere. But actually it’s quite
often that those errors don’t appear at all.
If we sum every pair of multiples of 0.01 up to 1.00 and look at
whether the printed result is too large (blue), too small (red), or
correct, we get a cool pattern:
Figure 1: How floating-point affects summing two multiples of 0.01, up
to 1.00
Where does this pattern come from?
Floats, briefly
A double-precision floating-point number
\(x\)
consists of 1 sign bit, 11 exponent
bits, and 52 fraction bits (in that order), for a total of 64 bits.
The sign bit provides a sign,
\(+\)
or
\(-\)
. The exponent bits represent
an integer
\(E\)
between −1022 and
1023, inclusive. The fraction bits represent a nonnegative integer
\(F\)
less than
\(2^{52}\)
, which corresponds to the
significand
\(1 + F/{2^{52}} \in [1,
2)\)
; that ever-present
\(1\)
is
called the “hidden bit”. The floating-point number’s value is
\(x = \pm 2^E(1 + F/{2^{52}})\)
.
The effective value of the last fraction bit is thus
\(2^{E-52}\)
, a quantity called the
ulp
, for “unit in the last place”, of
\(x\)
. The two floating-point numbers closest
to
\(x\)
differ from it by exactly one
ulp, except for an edge case on one side when
\(F = 0\)
and
\(x\)
is exactly a power of two. Example:
"hidden bit"
52 bits
float(0.1)  = 0.00011001100110011001100110011001100110011001100110011010₂
ulp(float(0.1)) = 0.00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000001₂
This description is good enough for our purposes but ignores many
other cases: 0, subnormal numbers, infinities, and NaNs; they use the
two values of exponent bits I didn’t describe. I also won’t consider
other precisions of floating-point numbers, for simplicity.
Anatomy of an addition
As an example (following e.g.
qntm
) let’s step through what
happens when you type
0.1 + 0.2
into the Python REPL.
1
First, the Python expression
0.1
evaluates to some
floating-point number: specifically, as required by the IEEE standard,
the nearest floating-point number to 0.1. We’ll write that
exact
number as
\(\text{float}(0.1)\)
.
2
Similarly, the Python expression
0.2
evaluates to some
other floating-point number,
\(\text{float}(0.2)\)
.
Now, we can imagine the
+
being evaluated in two steps.
First, Python computes the
exact
sum
\(\text{float}(0.1) + \text{float}(0.2)\)
.
Second, it rounds this to the nearest floating-point number. The
resulting value is
\(\text{float}(\text{float}(0.1) +
\text{float}(0.2))\)
. (This isn’t how it literally works — the
exact sum from the first step isn’t ever materialized anywhere — but
it’s mathematically accurate.)
Actually, there’s a subtlety here I did not notice until working this
out in excruciating detail:
\(\text{float}(0.1) + \text{float}(0.2)\)
is
equally close
to its two nearest floating-point numbers! When
this happens, Python rounds to the floating-point number with an even
significand, in this case up.
3
Finally, to print this value, Python has to convert it to a decimal.
This conversion is surprisingly subtle and not exactly specified by the
IEEE standard! Even though
\(\text{float}(\text{float}(0.1) +
\text{float}(0.2))\)
isn’t exactly 0.3, it is pretty close, so it
wouldn’t be unreasonable to display it as “0.3”. Another option would be
to display it exactly, as
“0.3000000000000000444089209850062616169452667236328125”. One might also
imagine displaying it after various amounts of rounding:
0.300000000000000044, or 0.30000000000000004441, or so on. One might
even consider, say, 0.30000000000000005, because it is still true that
\(\text{float}(\text{float}(0.1) +
\text{float}(0.2)) = \text{float}(0.30000000000000005)\)
; that
is, the Python expression
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.30000000000000005
is true. The subtlety of this conversion is evidenced by the fact that,
until a
specific patch in
Python 3.1
, if you typed
1.1
into the REPL, Python
would print your input back to you as
1.1000000000000001
.
The standard description of how this decimal conversion should work

Steele and White,
1990
4

The decimal representation should round-trip: if you type it in

49893519.article_summary: 文章解释了十进制小数在双精度浮点数中的表示与运算误差。以“0.1+0.2≠0.3”为例，介绍浮点数结构、ulp、输入与加法舍入，以及结果转为十进制显示的规则。文章进一步探讨为何金额相加时误差常不明显，并分析误差呈现特定图案的原因。
49893519.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：货币及小数计算中，浮点数、整数、Decimal 等表示方式的精确性、舍入问题，以及存储与展示的设计取舍。

不同观点：
• **整数（以分存储）更稳妥**：将金额按“分”转换为整数进行计算和存储，展示时再转为元/分，可避免二进制浮点误差。但若未来要求显示三位或更多小数，就可能需要调整存储逻辑。  
• **使用 Decimal 更具扩展性**：评论认为金额精度需求可能变化，因此直接使用十进制定点数比固定存储“分”更安全；不过在格式完全由自己控制的纯文本账本中，整数方案仍更方便。  
• **64 位浮点数未必实际有问题**：有人反驳“货币不能用浮点数”的常见说法，认为对现实金额而言，JavaScript 等使用的 64 位浮点数精度足以在最终结果四舍五入到分时满足需求。  
• **任何表示方式都无法消除业务舍入**：例如年费100美元，按月分摊时每月账单只能保留到分，全年相加可能少于100美元。争议焦点因此不仅是数据类型精度，也包括计费周期和舍入规则。

补充讨论：有人提到 Python 的分数类型及可构造实数，可支持更高或任意精度；另有评论仅指出页面图片先于文字加载、视觉上像1像素网格，属于界面体验问题，与核心技术讨论关系较弱。

data.title: SvelteKit 3
data.author: sampsn
data.article_summary: SvelteKit 3.0正式发布，整体延续此前框架体验，并提升了代码类型安全性、配置简洁度和错误处理能力。官方提供sv migrate命令，帮助迁移旧项目并生成待办清单；新项目可用sv create创建。主要变化包括配置迁移至vite.config.ts、$lib改为#lib、更强大的环境变量支持及更简洁的Service Worker。远程函数仍在开发中，预计需配合实验性Async Svelte使用。下届Svelte Summit将于11月在卢布尔雅那举行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Svelte/SvelteKit 新版本的价值、开发体验，以及在 AI 编程时代与 React、Vue、Solid 等方案的比较。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为 Svelte 更接近原生 HTML，代码可读性和开发体验好；SvelteKit 生产稳定、渐进改进，stores、双向绑定等功能简化开发，且比 Next.js 更令人愉悦。  
• Rich Harris 认为即使代理生成代码，框架仍影响最终质量：Svelte 可减少 JS 体积和 SSR 耗时，并重视可访问性、渐进增强；更高效的框架也能减少 AI token 消耗。  
• 多位用户表示现代 LLM 已能较好生成 Svelte 代码，配合 svelte-check 可快速完成项目；但也有人询问其“氛围编程”体验是否真的优于 React。  
• 反对或保留意见认为，Svelte 的自定义语法带来沉重的工具维护成本，JetBrains 插件支持差，开发者被迫依赖 VS Code；因此有人转向基于标准 TS/TSX 的 Solid。  
• 有人批评 Svelte 频繁“重新发明轮子”、版本变化大，也质疑 SvelteKit 的“+page.svelte”路由命名和嵌套目录设计。

补充讨论：案例显示 Svelte 可用于网站、桌面和移动端，Wails 下生成的应用体积小于 20MB。讨论还涉及全栈单体是否优于前后端分离，以及社区对 React、htmx 和破坏性升级标准不一致的质疑。

49926536.article_content:
Version 3.0 of SvelteKit, the official application framework for Svelte, is now available.
If you’ve used earlier versions of SvelteKit, everything will feel very familiar — it’s the same framework with a little more polish, a little more type safety, and a little less junk. We’ve made migration as seamless as we can with the
sv migrate
command...
npx
sv
migrate
sveltekit
-
3
--
tasks
all
--
confirm
...which will automatically migrate as much of your codebase as possible, and generate a TODO list for everything else. (If you’re agentically inclined, your robot friends will make short work of it.)
To create a
new
app, run
sv create
:
npx
sv
create
my
-
new
-
app
As with any major version bump there are a handful of breaking changes to be aware of, which are covered in the
migration guide
(or, more briefly, in the recent
release candidate announcement
).
Quick highlights:
configuration now lives in
vite.config.ts
instead of
svelte.config.js
the
$lib
alias is now
#lib
, making use of standard
subpath imports
environment variables
are more powerful and easier to use
service workers
are less boilerplatey
error handling is improved across the board
Are remote functions ready yet?
Not quite. But it’s our top priority!
Remote functions
are a set of utilities for secure, efficient, type-safe client-server communication. You’ve likely seen some version of this idea in other frameworks, but we think you’re going to prefer this one.
Using them requires
Async Svelte
, which for now requires an
experimental
flag. Bear with us.
Join us in Ljubljana next month
This is as good a place as any to remind everyone that the next in-person
Svelte Summit
is taking place on November 19-20 in the lovely town of Ljubljana, Slovenia. Among other things it will be a celebration of Svelte’s 10th birthday, and we’d love to share some cake with you.

data.title: Pi 1.0
data.author: sergiotapia
data.article_summary: 文章宣布 Pi 1.0 正式发布。它是一款强化、极简且可扩展的智能体框架，新增 Codemode、虚拟模型、延迟加载工具、缓存预热、会话中途系统消息、新主题及默认全屏等功能。同时推出实验性 Pi Durable，用于构建可长期运行、可灵活操控的智能体应用。两者均采用 MIT 许可并开放源码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pi 1.0 的定位、极简设计、可扩展性，以及其在本地运行、生产部署和个人工作流中的实际使用。

不同观点：
• 支持极简主义：用户认为较短的系统提示词适合性能有限的电脑，启动快、资源占用低；基础工具和按需扩展足以覆盖编码、个人管理及通用操作系统代理场景。  
• 看好通用化与可编程性：Pi 不应局限于“编码代理”，其工具原语、SDK、MCP 和模型无关设计便于构建 Slack 值班机器人、Telegram 服务及生产级代理；建议先交互式试用，再逐步完善 harness。  
• 质疑“极简”叙事：有人认为极简可能只是缺少功能的包装，项目成熟后仍会不断增加复杂度；但模块化设计即使最终走向全栈，也可能带来更好的底层架构。  
• 对工程体验的不同反馈：用户称赞 TUI、速度、扩展性及本地模型支持，也有人指出历史记录跳回、Kubernetes 会话持久化、JSONL 管理等问题。另有意见希望提供独立的 Anthropic 缓存预热包。  
• 资源与实现方式争议：有人希望用 Rust 等语言提供静态单文件、低内存版本，批评 TypeScript/Python 工具动辄占用近 1GB；hax 则被推荐为更纯粹的 shell 工具方案。  
• 社群与可信度：有人质疑“数十万用户”的说法，要求证据；也有人讨论 Tolkien 作品名称被科技公司反复使用的问题。

补充讨论：已有用户通过代理集中记录会话、分析模型和运行时评测；Pi Durable 被期待解决代理的持久执行问题。

Pi 1.0
Date:
Thu, 01 Oct 2026
From:
Earendil <
rfc@earendil.com
>
To:
You
Subject:
Pi 1.0
Today we are proudly shipping Pi 1.0: a hardened, minimal, extensible agent
harness that you can make your own. Hundreds of thousands of people around the
world use Pi every week. Many of you submit issues and pull requests. Over the
course of many months, we have used that feedback to improve, harden and evolve
Pi into a stable piece of software that people and businesses can depend on.
Pi is known for being minimal. We care about holding that line. While agentic
tooling changes every week, many of the changes do not last. Pi does not work
that way. We wait until something has proven itself, and only then do we
consider adopting it; weighing its true functionality against its inherent
added complexity. We spoke more about that process and how it relates to
Codemode and MCP earlier this week
here
.
The Pi 1.0 we are shipping today is a result of that process. Pi already ran
the latest models from every major provider, became a daily driver coding agent
for people around the world, and provided a supermalleable substrate on which
to build agentic applications. With Pi 1.0 we are adding the following into Pi:
Codemode (native support for MCP, and non-LLM models like Jev and image models)
Extension support for virtual models
Deferred tool loading
Cache warming for anthropic models
Mid-conversation system messages (transcript-aware prompt and tool changes)
A new TUI theme
Full-screen mode by default
We have thought about many of these features for months. They were thrown up
against the wall and stuck. The list of things that fell off the wall is much
longer. When we use Pi with all these new features it feels like a major step
forward, but it also still feels simple, like Pi.
Alongside this work of continually refining and evolving Pi, we also began to
understand that there were aspects of Pi that did not fit the shape of how many
people wanted to use it. At Earendil, we want to bring Pi's minimalism and the
way it allows you to wield AI outside of the coding agent and outside of the
terminal. It needs to be reachable from different surfaces and support
longer-running conversations and tasks. In short, Pi must become more durable.
Rather than stray from our minimal roots and try to make Pi something it
wasn't, we combined that work into a new experimental package that we are
shipping today, Pi Durable. Pi Durable is a new substrate for building
long-running agentic applications that lets the builders and the users of those
applications wield and steer the underlying intelligence with tremendous
dexterity. It shares Pi's key principles, minimalism and supermalleability, but
it extends those principles into new dimensions. Mario writes in more detail
about how we crafted Pi Durable
here
.

agency. Today we are shipping tools to you all to help do just that. We're

49926069.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pi 1.0 的定位、极简设计、可扩展性，以及其在本地运行、生产部署和个人工作流中的实际使用。

不同观点：
• 支持极简主义：用户认为较短的系统提示词适合性能有限的电脑，启动快、资源占用低；基础工具和按需扩展足以覆盖编码、个人管理及通用操作系统代理场景。  
• 看好通用化与可编程性：Pi 不应局限于“编码代理”，其工具原语、SDK、MCP 和模型无关设计便于构建 Slack 值班机器人、Telegram 服务及生产级代理；建议先交互式试用，再逐步完善 harness。  
• 质疑“极简”叙事：有人认为极简可能只是缺少功能的包装，项目成熟后仍会不断增加复杂度；但模块化设计即使最终走向全栈，也可能带来更好的底层架构。  
• 对工程体验的不同反馈：用户称赞 TUI、速度、扩展性及本地模型支持，也有人指出历史记录跳回、Kubernetes 会话持久化、JSONL 管理等问题。另有意见希望提供独立的 Anthropic 缓存预热包。  
• 资源与实现方式争议：有人希望用 Rust 等语言提供静态单文件、低内存版本，批评 TypeScript/Python 工具动辄占用近 1GB；hax 则被推荐为更纯粹的 shell 工具方案。  
• 社群与可信度：有人质疑“数十万用户”的说法，要求证据；也有人讨论 Tolkien 作品名称被科技公司反复使用的问题。

补充讨论：已有用户通过代理集中记录会话、分析模型和运行时评测；Pi Durable 被期待解决代理的持久执行问题。

data.title: CSS Bed: Classless CSS themes to use as starting points in web development
data.author: sea-gold
data.article_summary: CSS Bed 是一个收集无类（classless）CSS 主题的网站，可作为网页开发起点。用户只需将主题代码粘贴到 HTML 的 `<head>` 中即可使用。主题种类丰富，具备响应式、浏览器兼容性好、体积小、无需学习复杂类名等特点。页面还展示了表单、代码、表格、排版、链接及各类 HTML 元素效果，并提供 GitHub 源码和主题贡献入口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“无类（classless）CSS/极简 CSS 框架”作为网页开发起点的实用性、默认样式质量及发展趋势展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持无类 CSS：认为仅依靠 HTML 元素即可快速获得可用页面，适合作为起点；Pico.css、simple.css、tacit、w3c-chocolate、Bootstrap 等被认为能提供可靠基线，甚至可约束 LLM 生成过度复杂的 CSS。  
• 质疑“无类”限制：一旦需要细微布局调整，就必须引入类或其他非元素选择器；对于多页面项目，matcha.css 等贴近原生元素、但保留扩展能力的方案更实用。  
• 倾向自建可扩展方案：有人采用 reset.css、var.css、global.css、util.css、markdown.css 分层组织纯 CSS，以兼顾简单性和规模化。  
• 认为现有默认值不够好：不少主题在移动端缺少左右边距、导致横向滚动；字体排版、标题与段落间距等基础细节也常不合理。  
• 功能期待：dark mode 被认为应成为现代“合理默认值”；用户还希望能直接滚动浏览主题，而非逐个切换。  
• 现状与趋势：有人已多年使用 Tailwind，询问 normalize/reset.css 是否仍主流；也有人认为无类 CSS 可能借助 LLM 重新流行。

补充讨论：评论者还分享了 drop-in CSS、HTML3000 等类似项目，并指出个别链接存在异常跳转。

data.title: Several vulnerabilities have been discovered in the Linux kernel
data.author: luispa
data.article_summary: Debian于2026年9月29日发布安全公告DSA-6528-1，针对linux软件包修复大量安全漏洞，涉及2024至2026年公布的数百个CVE，可能影响内核及相关组件安全。建议Debian用户及时更新linux软件包，以降低攻击风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI加速软件漏洞发现后，开源项目和整个计算基础设施如何应对，以及CVE数量是否能真实反映安全风险。

不同观点：
• 乐观者认为，AI让更多人看到长期隐藏的问题，虽短期造成项目维护压力，但建立筛选、人工复核和定期修复流程后，能提升软件质量。小型项目称每月发现22个漏洞并可及时修复。  
• 悲观者认为，AI编程并未显著降低漏洞率，却大幅提高代码产量和安全研究速度，未来漏洞会持续激增，暴露计算基础设施的脆弱性。  
• 有人指出，AI生成“能运行”的代码与“安全”的代码之间存在明显差距；安全具有成本，若缺乏实际责任，软件公司往往不会主动承担。  
• 另一派质疑以CVE数量衡量问题：Linux对几乎所有可能影响内核安全的缺陷都谨慎分配CVE，因此“1313个漏洞”或CVE编号突破十万并不等于同等数量的严重漏洞。  
• 有评论要求补充漏洞是否可远程利用、是否仅本地提权等关键信息，认为单报数量不足以判断风险。

补充讨论：争议焦点是AI究竟主要带来安全收益还是风险扩张，以及人类过去未发现大量漏洞是否反映人工审查能力不足。评论还提到项目规模、代码质量与维护团队难以线性扩展，并建议统一版本规则，用不同版本号区分安全补丁、功能和系统性变更。

data.title: Using Opus 5.5 to discover a new eyewitness record of the dodo
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕大语言模型（LLM）在历史研究、资料处理、跨学科创新中的能力、局限及实际价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **效率与规模化研究价值**：Twiin称Opus 5.5处理了逾1万张二战档案图片，辅助破解1941年未破译的武装党卫军密码，并快速编写多个解码器；其价值在于跨语言处理和大幅降低研究成本，而非发现密码新漏洞。  
• **能力强但错误难以预测**：nl指出模型能完成高难度任务，却会犯“整体合理、局部错位”的非人类式错误，也不擅长判断发现的历史意义；并质疑文中表现是否属于较早版本。  
• **适合整理个人与冷门史料**：jamienk考虑扫描父亲的大量日记交给模型分析，体现人们希望借助AI挖掘未被理解的私人资料。  
• **对研究成果规模的质疑**：early_exit追问文本总页数，认为若仅从约3000页中找到渡渡鸟资料，筛选本身可能比发现内容更值得称道。  
• **跨学科促进新想法**：SV_BubbleTime赞同模型处于学科交界时更容易产生创新，类似让铁匠与面包师知识结合以改进炉子。  
• **补充性知识讨论**：Neil44纠正渡渡鸟仅生活在毛里求斯；dgellow则肯定文章质量。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AI究竟带来真正的研究突破，还是主要充当高效的资料整理、转录与筛选工具；其结论仍需人工验证。

data.title: Pi Durable
data.author: paulsmith
data.article_summary: Earendil与Pi社区发布Pi 1.0，并推出实验性框架Pi Durable。它不取代编码代理，而是用于构建可长期运行、跨环境、支持多人协作的智能体应用。该框架以存储和任务执行为核心，支持内存、SQLite、JSONL等后端及本地或远程执行环境，具备持久对话、故障恢复、上下文压缩和高度可定制等特点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Pi Durable 及类似“持久化 Agent harness”的架构、价值、实现难点与应用场景展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好持久化与云端迁移**：vito 介绍 Dagger agent，通过 OpenTelemetry 记录可重放的函数配方，使多沙盒状态可恢复、跨本地与云端迁移，支持长期、多 Agent、手机远程协作；lukebuehler 认为该方向具备耐久运行、故障恢复、监控、安全扩展和多人协作优势，行业正在趋同。
• **质疑状态一致性**：pulkitsh1234 关注 Agent 检查点与 VM、容器、浏览器等运行器状态如何同步；若 Agent 恢复但外部环境未恢复，可能产生“记忆已完成、实际未完成”的错位。
• **讨论数据模型取舍**：lemming 质疑 Durable 不支持真正的分支对话树，仅保留带祖先信息的 fork，认为这可能限制原有 Pi 能力，并追问是否是持久化保证所必需。

49925969.article_content:
Pi Durable
Date:
Thu, 01 Oct 2026
From:
Earendil Engineering <
rfc@earendil.com
>
To:
You
Subject:
Pi Durable
Today Earendil and the Pi community
shipped Pi 1.0
. This
reflects our belief that after countless hours of hardening, maintenance, and
active development, Pi is now a solid foundation on which to build. Pi also
continues to evolve. Together with Pi 1.0, we are shipping an experimental new
package called Pi Durable. Pi Durable was built specifically for long-running,
durable, and malleable agents that can run anywhere. We would like you to join
in the fun and help us make it the best durable harness there is.
Why Pi Durable?
Pi the coding agent is built to run on your (remote) machine, inside a terminal,
driven by one person. If the process dies, you look at what happened and tell it
to continue. That is what Pi 1.0 focuses on and excels at, and that is not
changing.
At Earendil, we want to bring this technology to everyone, in whatever form fits
their needs best. For that, we need a harness that runs anywhere, can be reached
from different surfaces, supports infinitely long conversations, survives
catastrophic internal and external failures, and lets multiple humans steer the
same agents.
Pi Durable is that harness. It does not replace the Pi coding agent. It is a
framework for building any agentic application, coding agents included. It
shares not only code with the Pi coding agent, like pi-ai, but also its
principles: minimalism and malleability.
It also lets us explore designs in this space without disrupting Pi the coding
agent. Lessons we learn building agentic applications on Pi Durable will flow
back into Pi the coding agent as they prove themselves valuable.
What is a harness?
Everybody has their own definition of a harness. We
wrote about this
previously
, but let us reintroduce the concept of
the harness for Pi Durable.
A harness is storage plus the machinery needed to run one or more conversations
with large language models in parallel. It provides the tools those models call,
and the execution environments the tools run in.
A conversation is an interaction between you and an agent, recorded as a
transcript. The agent is the large language model together with its settings,
like the thinking level, and the tools it can call.
Tools do their work through an execution environment, which can be your laptop,
a remote VM, or an in-memory sandbox. Which tools and which execution
environment an agent gets is up to each conversation.
Everything the harness runs, from calling the model to executing a tool, is a
task.
Like everything in Pi, Pi Durable is built so your agent can understand it. The
entire source code, without tests, is about 15,000 lines, which comes out to
about 150,000 tokens with GPT and about 250,000 with Claude. That's the worst
case. To build on Pi Durable, your agent rarely needs all of it; the storage
backends alone are 3,000 lines it can usually skip.
Now let us give you a little tour of Pi Durable, to illustrate what we built and
why we built it.
Long runs anywhere
We want agents to run for a long time and to be able to run anywhere, where
anywhere currently means anywhere there is a JavaScript runtime.
In Pi Durable, a harness opens over a storage backend. Pi Durable ships memory,
SQLite, and JSONL storage, plus a conformance suite and benchmarks for your own
backend. The SQLite and JSONL storage code uses no Node APIs, so with a small
adapter it runs on Bun or inside a Cloudflare Durable Object. The storage
interface is small and easy to implement on top of whatever you have, like a
key-value store or Postgres. One process owns a storage at a time, and other
clients attach to that process.
On SQLite, the harness only keeps the working set in memory: the active
transcripts, live tasks, and pending submissions. Everything else stays on disk
until it is needed. Active transcripts are naturally bounded by the model's
context window, because compaction summarizes older messages before they
overflow it. So even a conversation with tens of thousands of messages fits
snugly into memory.
Tools that need files or a shell get them from an execution environment. Pi
Durable ships a Node execution environment, which gives tools access to your
local files. Like storage, the execution environment interface is small and easy
to implement, so you can also expose remote execution environments to your
tools. That allows the harness to run on one machine while its tools run on
another. Your
env
function builds the environment for every tool call, from
the conversation's working directory, so each conversation can run in a
different place.

data.author: gumby

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：深海无氧高盐卤水池为何能长期保持清晰界面，以及其极端环境中的生命现象。

不同观点：
• [areoform]认为卤水池既美丽又反直觉，按扩散作用盐分应逐渐稀释，但这类水体似乎可持续数千年，关键物理机制并不直观。其引用数据表明：界面下盐度由40 PSU迅速升至160 PSU，溶解氧从180降至低于10 μmol/L；温度则缓慢升高约1℃，且不像是附近热液活动造成。  
• [areoform]隐含关注卤水池的稳定性与分层机制：盐度差可能形成明显的密度结构，使高盐卤水沉积并维持界面，但评论中未给出完整解释。  
• [nephihaha]将重点转向极端环境生命，惊叹在深海、近沸水、严寒及高空等环境中仍有微生物生存，强调生命适应性的广泛。  
• [ironqcold]仅表示对该现象感兴趣，未提出具体立场或论据。

补充讨论：评论之间没有直接争论，主要是“物理机制疑问”与“生命适应性惊叹”两条讨论线。争议焦点集中在：扩散为何未迅速破坏卤水池界面，以及盐度、密度和局部环境如何共同维持其长期稳定。

data.title: Git 3.0's upcoming SHA-256 default will be a costly mistake
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 文章认为，Git 3.0计划将默认哈希算法从SHA-1改为SHA-256，是代价高昂且收益有限的决定。虽然SHA-1理论上存在碰撞攻击，但现实中几乎不会造成实际威胁；迁移却会带来仓库兼容性、生态协作和全球基础设施的大规模成本。作者主张重新评估这一破坏性变更，避免不必要的“灾难”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Git 从 SHA-1 迁移至 SHA-256 的安全必要性、碰撞攻击实际风险，以及迁移的兼容性与成本展开。

不同观点：
• **SHA-1 已构成现实安全问题**：kpcyrd指出，2017年 SHAttered 已证明碰撞攻击可行；碰撞不仅影响一致性，也可能用于代码走私，即相同提交哈希对应不同代码。  
• **SHA-1只是内容标识，不是安全机制**：meinersbur援引 Linus 观点，认为 Git 哈希主要用于一致性检查，真正的信任应来自签名、分发渠道和 HTTPS；kazinator、OkayPhysicist则认为实际攻击场景有限，强化哈希未必解决认证问题。

Git 3.0's upcoming SHA-256 default will be a costly mistake
Git 3.0 will make SHA-256 the new default content hashing algorithm and it will be an incomprehensibly expensive and ultimately valueless and avoidable global nightmare.
Where to begin?
I've been sitting on this for a few years, mostly because there are smarter people who have been concentrating on this and I don't love being a back seat driver. However, I think that the Git 3.0 release is about to cost everyone a lot of time and angst for little benefit, and virtually nobody knows what's coming.
So grab some popcorn and let me tell you a tale of how one of the new upcoming Git 3.0
breaking changes
is about to be a huge, costly, global train wreck of a change for almost no practical value.
SHA-1 in Git Primer
I'll keep this short as many of you probably know this at a basic level.
Git is what's known as a content addressable database. This means that if you want to store and transmit data in it, Git will calculate a hash of the contents and use that in a key/value database as the key (the value being the content). The same content always gets the same hash, globally.
Git's use of SHA-1 hashes as keys in it's key-value object database
This is nice, because it means that the same file content is never stored twice. There is also a cool property where commits encode the hash of the commit that came before it, which means that this integrity essentially propagates - you can't change the hash of anything without changing the hash of everything that comes after it. This gives it "cryptographic integrity", meaning that hashing the latest commit essentially also hashes potentially millions of file contents, trees and commits that came before it.
In Git, this hash function has always been SHA-1. This was what Linus picked in 2005 when Git was started and it's worked pretty well for 20 years - it's relatively fast and impossible in a practical sense for two different files to accidentally hash to the same value.
In fact, as far as I'm aware, this has never happened in the history of every file, tree and commit ever made in Git in every repository ever created - billions and billions of them.
Mathematically, for SHA-1’s 160-bit output, the birthday bound means that you
would need about 1.4 septillion random files (1.4 quadrillion billion files -
1,400,000,000,000,000 billion - it's impossible to effectively describe) in a
single project
to have file hashes accidentally collide.
SHA-1 is Broken
There is a problem though, which is that mathematically, SHA-1 is now considered semi-"broken" because there have been published collision attacks (
SHAttered
in 2017,
SHA-1 is a Shambles
in 2020) - not really practical to exploit in any demonstrated way, but now theoretically possible.
So in response to this, after a huge amount of work by very smart people, the upcoming Git 3.0 release is planning to change it's default hashing algorithm from the semi-"broken" SHA-1 to the stronger SHA-256 algorithm.
But first, let's pause. Before we dig into this, what does "broken" mean?
This is important to understand, because it's probably not what normal people would think "broken" means. From a cryptographic hashing standpoint, broken in this sense essentially means that finding collisions
isn't impossible
.
In other words, if you throw enough money and GPUs at the problem, you can, for some content shapes, come up with two different things that hash to the exact same value, on purpose.
What can you do with a broken SHA-lor? Earl-y in the morrrrn...
This means that while it's still nearly impossible to
accidentally
have two reasonable files with different contents, it's not technically impossible to
manufacture
two different files that hash to the same thing.
This means that there theoretically exist attack vectors where someone could replace one file's contents with a malicious version and Git can't tell the difference because the hash is mathematically identical.
These papers showed that SHA-1 has a property that in theory can be exploited by modern GPU farms to produce purposeful collisions on the order of a few tens of thousands of dollars today that SHA-256 does not have (
google "linear message schedule sha-1 vs sha-256"
if you super-duper care...).
Sounds really scary and concerning, right?
Won't somebody please think of the children!?!
Collision attacks
Well, not really.
But let's take one minute to step back and talk about these collisions.
There are two main problems with hash functions when you're considering attacks on them (assuming I had to massively, stupidly, simplify things). One is a "collision attack" and the other is a "second-preimage attack".
A "collision attack" is when you know you're going to be an attacker but pretend to be a good guy until you gain trust. You generate two files on purpose with the same hash - one is benign and the other is malicious. You give people the benign one until you're trusted and then swit

Apple’s upcoming smart home camera is reportedly taking a very different approach to products from Ring and Google Nest, with the device designed to understand what is happening around the home without recording video for users to watch back.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, speaking on the new Power On podcast, says Apple’s camera will have “no video recording.” Instead, the device will use AI to analyze its surroundings and report what it detects.
The unusual approach could make privacy one of the defining features of Apple’s first dedicated home camera, while also making the product fundamentally different from a conventional security camera.
The device, known internally as J450, is expected to use a low-frame-rate camera alongside facial recognition and infrared sensors to identify people and pets around the home.
Rather than presenting a continuous or recorded video feed, it could provide information about activity in the house and use what it sees to power automations.
That could allow Apple’s Home system to recognize when someone enters or leaves a room, switch lights off when a room becomes empty, or adjust music and other settings depending on which household member is present.
Bloomberg has reported that Apple is planning a much broader push into smart home hardware
, beginning with its new HomePad hub, HomePod mini 2, and Apple TV 4K.
The Apple Post previously reported on the J450 camera as part of Apple’s wider smart home roadmap
, including its expected use of facial recognition and infrared sensing.
Gurman’s latest comments clarify an important part of how the camera could work: despite having a camera sensor, the product isn’t being designed around giving customers a library of recorded footage.
That would separate it from Apple’s existing HomeKit Secure Video system, which lets compatible third-party cameras securely stream and store encrypted recordings in iCloud.
It could also create limitations for customers who expect a security camera to provide footage after a break-in, package theft, or other incident. How Apple’s wider security system would handle those situations remains unclear.
Apple is reportedly developing a home security and monitoring service alongside the hardware, suggesting the J450 may be intended as one component of a larger system rather than a direct replacement for every traditional security camera.
The camera is expected to follow Apple’s initial HomePad launch rather than arrive alongside it this month, with previous Bloomberg reporting pointing to 2027 for Apple’s broader home security push.

data.title: ArXiv's Updated Rate Limit Policy
data.author: 50kIters
data.article_summary: 文章介绍，面对AI推动论文提交激增及低质量、拆分式和AI生成论文增加，arXiv自2026年10月1日起统一实行限流：每位作者每月最多提交2篇，同时最多保留3篇活跃投稿，且被拒稿件也计入额度。政策旨在公平分配志愿版主资源、减轻审核压力、保护论文库质量，并促使作者精选更具学术价值的成果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：arXiv因投稿量激增而实行按提交者限流，评论围绕政策合理性、学术质量、平台定位及潜在副作用展开。

不同观点：
• **支持限流**：认为按提交者而非作者计算较合理，不会过度影响大型合作团队；每月最多提交两篇、同时最多三篇，可缓解管理压力。投稿量从2016年9月的9,869篇增至今年同月40,363篇，并产生近9,000个支持工单，说明限流有现实必要。  
• **支持治理“AI slop”**：认为当前低质量、批量生成的AI论文泛滥，简单的速率限制能有效遏制；未来还可建立身份管理、垃圾投稿者黑名单及递进式限制。  
• **质疑过度管理**：指出arXiv本不应被视为质量认证，除移除违法内容外，强化审核可能误解其定位；真正的问题是高校过度依据论文数量、Google Scholar和h-index评价学者，应改革招聘晋升机制。  
• **担忧政策反效果**：认为高质量、高产作者也可能被限制，或被迫转向其他平台，使arXiv自我削弱、失去相关性。  
• **替代与扩展建议**：有人提出用仅保存元数据和文件哈希的聚合平台替代，以保留时间戳和引用功能；也有人希望大型会议取消绝对合著者人数限制。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“控制滥用”与“维护开放、低门槛发布”之间的平衡，以及限流应针对投稿行为，还是应从学术评价体系根治刷量动机。

Fair Moderation, Equitable Access, and AI: arXiv’s Updated Rate Limit Policy
By Kat Boboris
·
October 1
st
2026
arXiv, and the scientific community at large, are facing a watershed moment. Scholarly publishing is currently changing at a rapid pace, and we are seeing a massive transformation in how researchers communicate their results.
Before the advent of AI, there was an easily discernible, practical limit to the rate at which independent submissions could be produced, and arXiv’s volunteer moderators would limit submitters who were well above that threshold. With AI tools becoming more advanced and accessible to authors, the “practical limit” of how many papers can be submitted is now up for debate.
As of October 1st, 2026, arXiv is instituting an updated rate limiting policy across all submitters and categories as a stopgap while we determine what may be the new best practice for authors employing more and more advanced AI tools, and to give us time to improve our moderation tools and procedures accordingly.
Open access repositories across the board are seeing a sharp increase in the number of submissions per author, per month. In September of 2016, arXiv received 9,869 submissions. In September of 2024, arXiv received 20,569 submissions.
This September, arXiv received 40,363 submissions, which in turn generated almost 9,000 support tickets for arXiv staff and moderators.
In only the past two years, submissions have doubled.
arXiv submission rates have steadily increased since our founding in 1991. In September, arXiv received 40,363 submissions in a single month – a new record.
Advanced AI tools are helping drive these increases by making certain aspects of research faster and easier. arXiv policy permits authors to
employ AI as a tool in support of their research
as long as it is disclosed and the research meets arXiv’s standards of scholarly interest and advances the field of research. However, many of the submissions that arXiv is now receiving do not satisfy these requirements. Our moderators are observing an increase in thin papers of narrow scope, as well as ‘salami’ papers, where a single work is broken up and submitted as a set of smaller papers. There is also a marked increase in dense, AI-written papers. AI tools are making it easy for authors to flood arXiv and other repositories with these low-value papers.
Increases over the past two years in cs.AI (over 6X increase) illustrate the rate at which researchers are submitting to arXiv. Other arXiv categories have seen submissions double over the same period of time.
The heart of arXiv’s process for detecting and rejecting low-quality papers is our many volunteer moderators. We are so grateful that they donate their time and expertise every day. However, a relatively small proportion of authors are submitting a large number of low-quality papers and consuming a disproportionate fraction of the moderators’ time. This is unfair to authors who continue to submit quality papers — their papers can be delayed for days or weeks as a result.
Thomas Dietterich, Distinguished Professor Emeritus, Oregon State University and Chair of the arXiv Editorial Advisory Council
arXiv now limits submitters to up to two submissions per calendar month, with a limit of three total active submissions at any given time.
This policy update is being put into effect to equitably distribute our volunteer moderators’ time across arXiv authors, and protect the arXiv corpus from a sharp increase in inappropriate submissions.
Rate-limiting
is an established arXiv policy, with limiting originally primarily left to moderator discretion. arXiv has always asked that authors follow our codes of conduct and our submission guidelines. Articles submitted to arXiv must be of original, novel, and significant self-contained research that is relevant to arXiv categories. All submissions to arXiv must meet prescribed
scholarly standards
and be of
scholarly interest
to the scientific community. This policy update strives to fairly distribute the incredibly valuable work of our volunteer moderators who check that submissions meet these standards, and we hope it will also encourage authors to curate and submit only their best work to arXiv.
Frequently Asked Questions
If my paper is rejected, does it count towards my monthly total?
Yes – this rate limit is for submissions, not announced papers, because it is submissions that consume moderator time. If you submit two papers in a month, whether they are accepted or rejected, you will have to wait until the next month to submit to arXiv again. We want to encourage authors to be mindful with their work, taking care that they are submitting something substantial of scholarly interest that meets arXiv’s guidelines and standards.
What if my submissions are in different subject areas?
This rate limit applies to all submissions, across all categories.

• **替代与扩展建议**：有人提出用仅保存元数据和文件哈希的聚合平台替代，以保留时间戳和引用功能；也有人希望大型会议取消绝对合著者人数限制。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“控制滥用”与“维护开放、低门槛发布”之间的平衡，以及限流应针对投稿行为，还是应从学术评价体系根治刷量动机。

data.title: Vote on which of Hacker News' challenges for AI have been met
data.author: stabbles
data.article_summary: 页面提示这是最后一条评论，可查看相关结果；评论内容正在加载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕历年“AI能力预测”是否已实现、测试标准是否清晰，以及AI进步的范围与局限展开讨论。

不同观点：
• [hatthew]认为自己的“最后考试”并未通过：AI只完成其六项要求中的一项（解决Navier–Stokes问题），17%不及格；且网站摘要遗漏内容并把“且”误写成“或”。
• [joegibbs]承认预测失误：原以为AI还需20年才能根据提示可靠构建并部署任意应用，实际提前约18年实现。
• [ben_w]认为自己的预测被证伪，但强调LLM仍不能高效、无错误地完成任意新任务；会写代码不等于具备通用能力。
• [AngryData]认为公众高估LLM，指出其常编造内容、伪造来源，在硅胶、农业、建筑、机械等专业问题上可能给出危险答案；代码并非最难任务。
• [Retr0id]指出AI仍难识别或生成ASCII足部图，质疑相关测试已通过；[mrweasel]则认为人类本身也常无法区分AI，传统图灵测试可能低估了人类判断缺陷。
• [ErrantX]观察到测试主题从“写代码、点咖啡”转向开门、模拟人性、科学突破，反映期待显著升级。

补充讨论：多人批评预测目标含糊、投票标准不清；题目过多导致参与者弃读。有人建议增加“按争议排序”，并追问网站内容、整理和部署使用了多少AI。

data.title: Aweb – Communication for AI Agents
data.author: gurjeet
data.article_summary: aweb是一个MIT许可、可自托管、支持联邦的AI代理通信系统，为代理提供稳定身份、持久邮件与聊天、消息唤醒、历史记录、权限控制和跨服务器通信。它独立于运行时，支持Claude Code、Pi及其他可消费事件流的环境；消息即使代理离线也能可靠保存和投递。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 AWeb（可能支持代理间及人-代理通信）的用途、命名、成本、安全性，以及代理协作中的风险展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好通信与协作价值**：owenthejumper认为，AWeb不应局限于“代理对代理”，也可实现人与代理之间的实时协作，例如通过自托管沙盒接入Slack。  
• **质疑命名缺乏检索与避嫌**：binaryturtle指出“AWeb”早已是Amiga系统的知名浏览器名称，认为发布前通过DuckDuckGo或Google检索即可避免品牌冲突。  
• **质疑价格和性价比**：maxdo认为其单条消息价格相较AWS、Modal、Cloudflare等普通服务高出上千倍；对内部使用而言，自行开发可能更便宜且更安全。  
• **关注已有类似项目**：etaioinshrdlu提到“ch.at”已升级为支持代理消息的版本，甚至仍可通过DNS使用，暗示AWeb并非首创。  
• **作者积极回应**：juanre自称AWeb的开发者，感谢发布并表示愿意回答问题。  
• **担忧代理串通**：jamsuv-vapXy1-d询问该系统是否能防止代理之间相互串通，涉及安全、治理和滥用风险。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是AWeb相较既有方案的独特价值、定价合理性、命名冲突，以及能否有效控制代理协作带来的安全问题。

MIT licensed

federated

self-hostable
Communication for AI agents.
aweb
gives agents stable identities, durable mail and chat, and wake-up events across sessions, runtimes, and machines. Independently operated servers can federate with one another.
The CLI and API are runtime-independent. Maintained wake-up integrations are available for Claude Code and Pi; other runtimes can consume the event stream.
Install the CLI
npm install -g @awebai/aw
In the agent’s directory
aw init
CLI tutorial →
View source →
Ask an agent to evaluate it
Read https://aweb.ai/llms.txt and explain how aweb would fit my current agent setup. If it fits, set it up with me.
llms.txt
contains the same product and setup information in plain text.
Example
Incoming work wakes the agent.
Alice runs in Claude Code. Bob runs in Pi on another machine. Alice sends a message;
aweb
stores it, wakes Bob through the Pi extension, and delivers Bob’s reply to Alice. If Bob is offline, the message waits until he returns.
alice
Claude Code · machine A
aw mail send --to bob --subject "review my branch" --body-file note.md
message_id: 01J9GX52…
● aweb — reply from bob: "review my branch"
aweb
server
replied
bob
Pi · machine B
offline
● aweb — mail from alice: "review my branch"
aw mail show --message-id 01J9GX52…
aw mail reply 01J9GX52… --body-file reply.md
message_id: 01J9GYEM…
The message is durable server state. A wake-up event tells the runtime that work is waiting; the agent then fetches the message by ID.
Replay
The real thing, recorded 2026-09-05, no cuts:
aw init
, invite, join; alice in Claude Code, bob in Pi with the
aweb
extension; the operator asks alice a question only bob can answer; she asks him over
aw chat
, his session wakes with the verified question, reads the file and answers in nine seconds; she reports and closes;
aw chat history
shows the exchange. 95 seconds. Using beads?
bd mail
through
aweb
→
When the sender needs an immediate answer, chat waits for the recipient:
aw chat send-and-wait bob "is retry state per call or per session?"
● bob: per call — session state stays.
Maintained wake-up integrations
Claude Code channel
how →
claude plugin marketplace add awebai/claude-plugins
claude plugin install aweb-channel@awebai-marketplace
Install once. Then start Claude Code with the channel loaded and permission prompts off:
claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:aweb-channel@awebai-marketplace
Incoming mail and chat are then presented inside the session. Channel messages reach the session only in bypass-permissions mode today; in the default auto mode they arrive and are not shown. Claude Code asks once to confirm the development-channels flag.
Full setup →
Pi extension
how →
pi install npm:@awebai/pi@latest
Install once; Pi wakes when mail, chat, or tasks arrive.
aweb for Pi →
Other runtimes use the same
event stream
.
Why aweb
Identity, delivery, wake-up, and federation.
aweb
provides identity, authentication, durable delivery, wake-up, message history, access control, and federation.
Install the CLI and run
aw init
to give an agent an identity and connect it. Start with two agents; add machines, teams, and organizations without replacing the communication layer. The same addresses and protocol continue to work as the system grows.
Because addressing and federation are open, an agent can communicate beyond the server or organization where it began.
Scope
Use the agents you choose.
Any agent that can call the CLI, HTTP API, MCP tools, or event stream can use
aweb
.
aweb
stores and delivers messages, maintains identity and addressing, and emits delivery and wake-up events.
Properties
Durable, controlled, and federated.
Durable messaging
Messages are server state, not session scrollback. A message remains available after either agent’s session ends and while the recipient is offline. Fetch any message later by ID.
Wake-up events
A delivery event signals that work is waiting. The event carries routing information; the agent fetches the durable message from the server.
Stable identity
An addressed agent keeps its identity when its session, process, software, or machine changes. Private signing keys stay with the agent or its chosen custodian.
Controlled delivery
An agent can accept first contact from any verified sender or restrict delivery to verified team members and explicit contacts. Team membership is carried by signed certificates.
Federation
Organizations can operate separate servers and exchange signed messages. They do not need a shared account, runtime, or model provider.
Open source
The aweb server, AWID registry, and aw CLI are MIT licensed. The hosted service runs the same communication server that can be run independently.
Identity and authority
AWID separates identity authority from message delivery.

domain/name

data.title: Bez: Generating a browser engine from specs and tests
data.author: nerdypepper
data.article_summary: 该页面介绍了 burrito.space 的 bez 开源仓库。项目以 Rust 为主，包含浏览器布局、CSS 规范兼容性测试、基准测试、Oracle、自动修复与任务流水线等模块，重点覆盖宽高比、定位、浮动、层叠、滚动条、设备像素取整等 CSS 特性。仓库持续开发，已有约1200次提交，并通过多个专题分支和实验追踪兼容性与性能改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用网页标准和 AI/自动生成技术构建浏览器，并探讨其可行性、兼容性及扩展应用。

不同观点：
• 乐观设想：Alacart认为，庞大的 Web 标准理论上足以生成浏览器；若减少人工实现规范的工作，便可投入更多精力完善规范，形成正向循环。但其后补充称这是愿景，当前技术距离实际落地仍远。  
• 谨慎质疑：esprehn指出，规范主要描述可观察行为，存在大量由浏览器自行决定的模糊地带；要真正兼容 Web，可能仍需复现 Chrome 等主流实现，而非只依赖规范。AI还应通过比较 Chromium、其他引擎及 Ladybird 源码来发现差异和优化。  
• 对可控性的期待：fouc希望未来浏览器在各方面都能被程序完全控制，并期待摆脱 Chromium/Blink 生态。  
• 应用扩展：mircerlancerous认为该思路可将 Web 应用转为原生应用，并加入 WebView 不具备的原生功能。  
• 可理解性与泛化疑问：有人质疑生成出的代码是否能被人理解，并追问能否用类似方法运行 MacOS、iOS；“能否跳舞”则是对实际能力的调侃。  
• 其他：有人询问项目名称是否源自 Jev，反映对命名规范的关注。

补充讨论：核心争议在于“从规范自动生成浏览器”是现实可行的工程路径，还是受规范歧义、历史兼容性和实现细节限制的长期愿景。

主要讨论点：利用网页标准和 AI/自动生成技术构建浏览器，并探讨其可行性、兼容性及扩展应用。

不同观点：
• 乐观设想：Alacart认为，庞大的 Web 标准理论上足以生成浏览器；若减少人工实现规范的工作，便可投入更多精力完善规范，形成正向循环。但其后补充称这是愿景，当前技术距离实际落地仍远。  
• 谨慎质疑：esprehn指出，规范主要描述可观察行为，存在大量由浏览器自行决定的模糊地带；要真正兼容 Web，可能仍需复现 Chrome 等主流实现，而非只依赖规范。AI还应通过比较 Chromium、其他引擎及 Ladybird 源码来发现差异和优化。  
• 对可控性的期待：fouc希望未来浏览器在各方面都能被程序完全控制，并期待摆脱 Chromium/Blink 生态。  
• 应用扩展：mircerlancerous认为该思路可将 Web 应用转为原生应用，并加入 WebView 不具备的原生功能。  
• 可理解性与泛化疑问：有人质疑生成出的代码是否能被人理解，并追问能否用类似方法运行 MacOS、iOS；“能否跳舞”则是对实际能力的调侃。  
• 其他：有人询问项目名称是否源自 Jev，反映对命名规范的关注。

补充讨论：核心争议在于“从规范自动生成浏览器”是现实可行的工程路径，还是受规范歧义、历史兼容性和实现细节限制的长期愿景。

data.title: Automatic Transmission – a data-privacy study of connected vehicles
data.author: rafaelc
data.article_summary: 文章研究联网汽车及配套App的隐私风险，重点探讨传输的个人数据、接收方及厂商回应。研究人员于2024年10月至2025年8月测试美国市场21辆汽车和30款App，通过Wi‑Fi、蜂窝网络及抓包分析数据流向，并评估车辆在静止、驾驶和隔绝蜂窝信号等情境下的通信行为。研究指出，数据离开设备后消费者几乎失去控制，企业可能将其分享或出售给未披露的第三方。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新车车载遥测、数据收集与隐私控制，尤其是车主能否真正退出，以及相关技术和监管问题。

不同观点：
• 隐私担忧者认为，多数新款小型车会持续上传驾驶、位置等数据，退出机制不透明，甚至可能因缺少数据导致保险加价；车主被迫在接受协议、放弃远程启动等联网功能或不用车之间选择。  
• 实用主义者主张直接关闭联网功能，例如拔掉通信模块保险丝；已有车主这样做，也有人希望形成合法的第三方禁用设备市场。  
• 另一些人倾向购买老车，认为老款福特、Scion等没有遥测、易维修，能避免数据收集。  
• 有评论认为问题不能归咎消费者，公众需要提高隐私意识并推动立法；目前消费者往往“懂技术但不懂隐私”。  
• 个别品牌被视为相对友好：本田减少向第三方提供精确位置；特斯拉虽有隐私设置，但其实际效果尚未充分验证。斯巴鲁在部分州因维修权规定而被迫禁用联网系统。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“联网功能可关闭”是否等于“车辆不再上传数据”，以及拔除模块是否会影响车辆正常使用。评论还质疑车企、保险公司和第三方广告/追踪分析公司如何使用这些数据，并指出消费者常常不知道车辆依赖手机、服务器乃至境外网络才能运行。

Research Questions
Photo is not loading
images/car-diagram.png
Connected Vehicle Ecosystem
This diagram shows the data flows to and
from a vehicle and its companion mobile app.
Both devices send data, including private consumer data, to different 1st and 3rd party servers using Wi-Fi and cellular service.
Solid arrows represent flows that were intercepted through our experiments.
The  Problem
Once the data gets sent to these servers, it is up to the companies that receive the consumer information to
make decisions on what they do with it. Unfortunately, in many cases, this includes
sharing or selling consumer data to other undisclosed 3rd parties.
Consumers have no control over their data once it has left their device
In this paper, we take the first steps to address the limited visibility into the privacy implications of the connected vehicle ecosystem.
We identify two vantage points in the ecosystem where we can gain insight into the data that connected vehicles
are sharing with both manufacturers and third parties: the vehicles
themselves and the mobile apps provided by manufacturers.
We ask the following guiding questions:
01
What personal consumer data do connected vehicles and their companion mobile apps transmit?
02
Who receives that personal consumer data?
03
What is the manufacturer response to these findings?
Methods
We investigated 21 vehicles from the U.S. market in a controlled
environment along with 30 companion mobile apps instrumented
with on-site vehicles between October 2024 and August 2025. Below is a description of the experiments we ran and our setup.
Vehicle Testing
Photo is not loading
images/rpi.png
Wi-Fi Testing Setup
To collect Wi-Fi traffic from vehicles,
we configured a custom access point (AP) on a Raspberry Pi and
used tcpdump to log all packets that were sent or received via this
AP.
This allowed us to see all the destinations the vehicles were sending data to but not the information within the packets as it was encrypted.
Photo is not loading
images/test-facility.jpg
Stationary Tests
Idle Baseline
vehicle on â no activity
Active Test
perform all possible actions
Driving Test
drive 5â45 mph with acceleration & hard braking
Isolating Cellular Traffic
Photo is not loading
images/faraday-tent.jpg
One hypothesis we tested was whether
blocking a vehicleâs ability to communicate over its cellular network
would force more Wi-Fi communication. To block external cellular
signals, we drove 11 EVs in the sample into a car-sized Faraday tent providing â93 dB of attenuation, blocking their
cellular connection entirely. Stationary Idle and Active tests were repeated inside the tent to see whether
traffic that normally goes out over cellular rerouted to Wi-Fi instead.
App Testing
In total, we experimented with 30 connected vehicle
companion apps that were paired with the vehicles at
Consumer Reportsâs testing facility.
Device Setup
01
We used a combination of test phones and iOS versions for our
experiments: an iPhone 8/iOS 16.6, an iPhone X/iOS 16.7.11, and an
iPhone 13/iOS 18.5.
02
To minimize background traffic, we deleted all
non-essential apps on the test phones and tested apps one-by-one,
including deleting each vehicle app and restarting the phone before
downloading the next app.
03
We used the iOS native screen recording
feature to record our interactions with each app for later review.
04
To capture and decrypt network traffic from
the companion mobile apps, we used iPhones with custom root certificates connected
to mitmproxy.
Process for Testing Each App
01
During app installation and login we accepted all permission requests (e.g., tracking,
location, calendar access, Bluetooth, notifications) that the application requested
02
We had a Consumer Reports employee log into the app using
their existing credentials associated with a vehicle on the lot.
03
Once we were logged-in, we manually exercised
all available functionality, such as looking for nearby charging staions, geolocating the vehicle, viewing vehicle data and service
history (e.g., tire pressure), viewing notifications (e.g., âdoors are
unlockedâ), and viewing in-app privacy policies.
04
Some apps allowed
us to perform physical interactions on the vehicle, such as remotely
opening the trunk. We performed all such actions and verified that
the vehicle completed each request.

主要讨论点：围绕模型路由器的能力、效果、成本控制、兼容性及训练方法展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **性能与模型选择**：YuechenLi认为应比较 GPT-6.1 Sol 与“GPT-6 Astra + DeepSeek”方案；其测试显示 6.1 Sol 更省 token、编程表现接近 Astra，Astra 的明显优势主要在视觉和空间推理领域。  
• **路由效果与竞品比较**：thefourthchime询问其内部路由机制与 Cursor Auto Mode 的差异；jamesforestwest进一步关注如何划分模型桶，以及任务超出所选模型能力时的处理方式。  
• **训练方法的局限**：svnt质疑若路由器训练数据由前沿模型标注，除降低成本、将简单任务交给便宜模型外，如何超越前沿模型性能。  
• **模型与部署兼容性**：有人询问是否支持 GitHub Copilot、OpenRouter 及任意模型提供商，也关心能否接入本地或局域网部署的 Qwen 等开源模型，以及为何自托管仍需要 OpenRouter。  
• **供应商质量控制**：ajspig1关注 OpenRouter 上开源模型不同供应商造成的性能差异，以及路由器能否识别供应商降级并动态调整。  
• **成本与开放性**：用户询问是否支持预设预算、训练模型是否开放权重。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是路由器能否真正提升性能，还是仅通过任务分流实现成本优化；另有用户以“AGI 已到来”表达对项目的高度评价，但缺乏具体论据。

data.title: Butterflies use optical illusions to dodge predators
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 埃克塞特大学与埃塞克斯大学在《自然》发表研究称，蝴蝶翅膀上的条纹和斑点会与飞行方式共同制造视觉错觉，干扰鸟类等捕食者对速度和方向的判断，使其在最后攻击瞬间偏离目标。研究解释了蝴蝶虽色彩醒目，却较少被空中捕食者捕获，表明翅膀图案可能是重要的生存适应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：蝴蝶翅膀图案如何在飞行和捕食过程中产生视觉误导，以及相关实验的可视化证据。

不同观点：
• **证据展示取向（yathern）**：对研究方法感兴趣，尤其希望看到高速摄影记录的“旋转木马/ barber-pole effect”，或志愿者在触屏上捕捉虚拟蝴蝶的实验视频，以直观验证图案对捕食者的影响。  
• **拟态与伪装类比（scun）**：将这种视觉干扰现象类比为“炫目伪装”（dazzle camouflage），认为其核心是通过复杂图案扰乱观察者对运动方向、轮廓或位置的判断。  
• **生物智能的延伸解读（anthk）**：认为研究结果令人震撼，并联想到 Michael Levin 的观点，即生物体中非常微小、离散的组成部分也可能表现出某种“智能”或协调能力。这一观点超出了蝴蝶伪装实验本身，属于更宏观的理论联想。

补充讨论：评论之间没有直接争论，主要形成了“希望看到实验依据—将现象联系到伪装机制—进一步上升到生物智能”的递进关系。争议焦点潜在在于：蝴蝶图案究竟只是被自然选择塑造的视觉伪装，还是可被解释为更广义的局部生物智能。

Butterflies use optical illusions to dodge predators
News
Butterflies use optical illusions to dodge predators
Date
Wed 30 Sep 26
A bird attacking a butterfly will often find its beak snapping at thin air.
According to new research, that split-second miss isn't just bad luck. It's caused by a visual illusion from the butterfly's wings.
The new study – published in the journal Nature, by the University of Exeter and the University of Essex – provides the first evidence that a butterfly's flight and wing pattern work together to create powerful visual illusions that scramble a predator's sense of speed and direction, making them misdirect attacks.
It helps solve a long-standing puzzle - butterflies have striking patterns that make them stand out, yet remarkably few predators specialise in catching them mid-flight.
Moths, by contrast, are hunted by a wide range of visually guided aerial predators.
"The stripes and spots on many butterflies’ wings interfere with the way visual systems try to guess the direction and speed of moving things, boosting false motion cues while hiding the butterfly's true heading," said Dr George Hancock, from the University of Exeter's Centre for Ecology and Conservation on the Penryn Campus in Cornwall.
"The illusions interfere with the predator’s most basic visual targeting system and disrupt the final ‘ballistic attack’ in the tens of milliseconds when it commits to grabbing its prey, with no time to change course.
"As a result, birds and other predators will often simply miss."
Dr Anna Hughes
, from the
Department of Psychology
, at the University of Essex added: "Butterflies’ beautiful wings are not just for show, they are vital for survival.
"Our brains – and those of other animals - don’t always interpret visual information perfectly, leading to illusions.
"We show this might have important consequences in the natural world, and in particular for butterflies, their striking patterns may have evolved to create confusing motion signals when in flight, making it difficult for predators to make accurate attacks."

• **证据展示取向（yathern）**：对研究方法感兴趣，尤其希望看到高速摄影记录的“旋转木马/ barber-pole effect”，或志愿者在触屏上捕捉虚拟蝴蝶的实验视频，以直观验证图案对捕食者的影响。  
• **拟态与伪装类比（scun）**：将这种视觉干扰现象类比为“炫目伪装”（dazzle camouflage），认为其核心是通过复杂图案扰乱观察者对运动方向、轮廓或位置的判断。  
• **生物智能的延伸解读（anthk）**：认为研究结果令人震撼，并联想到 Michael Levin 的观点，即生物体中非常微小、离散的组成部分也可能表现出某种“智能”或协调能力。这一观点超出了蝴蝶伪装实验本身，属于更宏观的理论联想。

补充讨论：评论之间没有直接争论，主要形成了“希望看到实验依据—将现象联系到伪装机制—进一步上升到生物智能”的递进关系。争议焦点潜在在于：蝴蝶图案究竟只是被自然选择塑造的视觉伪装，还是可被解释为更广义的局部生物智能。

data.title: The death of web development education
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 文章讨论生成式AI对网页开发教育、技术出版和内容创作者的冲击。聊天机器人取代人工学习与交流，抓取并无偿重述原创内容，导致博客、课程、书籍和视频流量及收入大幅下降。许多教育者、技术作者和开发者因此关闭业务、下线作品或转行，优质免费内容的创作激励也随之减弱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成式AI对教育、技术学习及EdTech商业模式的冲击，以及学习者、教师和内容创作者应如何适应。

不同观点：
• **AI提升学习效率**：AI可即时答疑、个性化出题和跟踪进度，用户认为其优于“照本宣科”的教师；重复记忆API、日志表等低价值训练可被淘汰，教育应转向领域理解、系统设计、评估和权衡。
• **教育行业必须转型**：行业受冲击是技术变革的常态，应转型或改行。未来开发者教育应强调拆解问题、验证AI输出、调试、安全性和可维护性，而非单纯写代码。
• **人类内容仍有价值**：部分创作者称课程、书籍能提供系统性、深度学习，LLM容易让人跳过真正学习；高质量人工内容、互动体验和实践仍可能形成竞争力。
• **AI带来创作与教学增益**：教师利用AI制作互动案例、游戏和课程，但担忧高级技能被“速度优先”取代，数据分析仍需人在回路中。
• **学习内容价值存在争议**：有人认为课程/书籍销售下滑主要源于AI；也有人认为失业、初级岗位减少和工资下降才是原因，或认为许多视频本就存在大量填充内容。
• **AI辅助编程的边界**：有人认为AI结合简洁技术可减少无谓复杂度；另一方强调应保持代码理解和架构控制，避免让代理做关键决策。

补充讨论：争议核心是AI究竟替代教育内容与教师，还是仅改变教学形式；同时也涉及盗版、流量激增、内容创作者收入下降及教师岗位前景。

49927100.article_content:
molily
Navigation
In a personal blog post,
Baldur Bjarnason describes
how he worked in various fields and positions: as an author, publisher, consultant, developer, educator, as well as radio and TV producer. None of these jobs were economically viable in the long term.
Adding insult to injury, the respective communities alienate interdisciplinary people who do not fit into their narrow conception of the field. For example, either you are considered as too “technical” for a “creative” job or too “creative” for “technical” job.
Bjarnason describes the impact of generative AI on web development education:
[All] my training and education projects had dropped off one by one. Most of my peers who had been selling courses and training were shutting down their businesses. The demand for web dev ebooks had cratered. […]
Software developers haven’t all switched to using agents for their coding, but they do seem to have all switched to error-prone, backwards-facing, nondeterministic chatbots for what now passes as web dev “education”.
Many independent educators who used to earn a living from web development training and developer relations have reported that GenAI has ruined their business.
Axel Rauschmayer
is one of the world’s most prolific writers on JavaScript and TypeScript. He used to
publish his e-books as free online books
. Since 2005, he has explained the details of ECMAScript and other web technologies in his influential blog
2ality
. Now he writes:
The income from my book sales went from being enough for me to live off (2024) to zero (2026).
The traffic to my blog and my books (which were free to read online) increased beyond what I can currently afford. Virtually all of it comes from AI crawlers, so there is no ad income.
Therefore, I’m taking my blog and my books offline so that I can decide what to do next – especially w.r.t. AI companies stealing my work.
(
Rauschmayer still sells his books on JavaScript and TypeScript for a reasonable price!
)
Salma Alam-Naylor used to work in Developer Relations
, a role under constant pressure to justify its existence. Companies expect DevRel to generate short-term financial gain – which it cannot by nature. This lead Alam-Naylor to burnout and anxiety. In this situation, she writes that
AI is killing developer education
:
[Developers] aren’t gathering together in online spaces to learn and teach and share exciting projects anymore, rather they are mindlessly scrolling for a much-needed hit of short-form content dopamine (because the horrors of the world are more persistent than ever). […] [Many] developers have replaced authentic human collaboration with conversations with the dreaded Chat Bots. […]
The future feels bleak for educators. Rich curriculums we craft intentionally and carefully for real human audiences are now routinely stolen and regurgitated by predictive algorithms. The Chat Bots, with their sycophantic tone of voice, are deliberately engineered to erase our own personalities, hard work and craft entirely from the equation.
The only conclusion I can draw from this is that my experience, skills, empathy and teaching expertise no longer hold the value they once did in this volatile industry (if they ever really did?).
Alam-Naylor decided to accept a lower-paid developer job without public exposure. She decided to go offline.
She cites
Josh W. Comeau
, who creates online courses, well-researched articles and interactive tutorials on web technologies. GenAI has
destroyed his business model as well
:
I’ve spoken to a few course creators now, and we’re all seeing the same trend. Revenue down 50%+. Fewer people engaging with our content. People switching to LLMs, which slurp up all of our work and regurgitate it, without consent or compensation.
Comeau notes
that with LLMs,
there’s no incentive for people to make high-quality free content.
YouTube content creator
Kyle Cook from
Web Dev Simplified
reported that the views on his programming tutorials and thereby his income
essentially dropped by half
.
I’m making half the money I was making exactly one year ago. [This] is definitely not sustainable for a full-time job. […] [There’s] almost no incentive as a creator of content to create programming content when it makes practically no money and is incredibly difficult to make when I could just make a video about the latest AI model, which is easy to make, makes more money, and gets more views. […] There’s almost no reason to make programming content anymore. The only reason I do it is because I find value in it. I find enjoyment in it. And I’m able to make money through other means rather than just YouTube ad revenue.

is a renowned technical writer and editor of many books and articles on web topics. In a
series of blog posts
, she reflects on the impact of GenAI on technical publishing. She reports that GenAI has

data.author: suopspaces

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕约翰·冯·诺伊曼的学术影响、个人轶事、历史评价及相关读物展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 高度评价其影响力：有人认为他在20世纪科学、数学及计算机等众多领域的基础性贡献，整体上超过爱因斯坦和普朗克；也有人感叹其名字在学习中反复出现，或称其为“最重要的科学家之一”。
• 关注其非凡个性：评论提到他能与三岁孩子平等交谈、记忆力惊人，但也有“开车时沉迷阅读、近乎自毁”的轶事，展现其天才与生活习惯的反差。
• 对晚年经历存在质疑：有人认为相关介绍“美化”了生命末期，引用弗里曼·戴森《Birds and Frogs》，称冯·诺伊曼晚年健康状况恶化，甚至无法正常完成学术演讲。
• 将其与当代技术联系：有人借其“快速理解和超强记忆并非持久影响”的评价，讨论人工智能在数学中的作用；另有人提及“冯·诺伊曼架构”的署名与贡献归属争议。
• 推荐传记与文学作品：《The Man from the Future》《The MANIAC》，以及关于其助手职责的文章；还介绍了包括冯·诺伊曼在内的匈牙利“火星人”科学家群体。

补充讨论：评论整体以敬仰和趣闻分享为主，也夹杂资源推荐、历史补充及战争与计算机硬件相关的黑色幽默。

data.title: Supabase Is Acquiring Turso
data.author: cvburgess
data.article_summary: Supabase宣布收购Turso，双方将共同打造面向AI代理的新一代数据库基础设施。Supabase继续以Postgres为核心，Turso继续发展SQLite。Turso通过Rust重构SQLite及云平台，实现按需、低成本管理数百万数据库，适合代理原型开发，并可随业务增长接入Postgres生产环境。收购后Turso保持运营，双方将共同推进开源与代理基础设施建设。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Turso项目及其与SQLite的关系、商业可持续性、性能质量和未来发展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 担忧项目未来：有人希望SQLite及Turso重写版本在LLM驱动的小型应用中胜出，但担心Turso托管业务收入不足，影响项目持续性；也有人担忧此次变化会损害现有客户利益。  
• 对未来持乐观态度：部分用户认为项目不再完全依赖Turso公司的成败，反而降低了技术选型风险，未来可能更愿意采用Turso。  
• 认可实际使用体验：用户反馈Turso在小型项目及Rust异步应用中运行良好、性能很不错，希望后续变化不会影响现有体验。  
• 关注性能与稳定性：有人希望新团队投入更多资源修复问题，指出Turso曾多次尝试加入ClickBench测试却不断暴露新Bug，性能不应比SQLite慢数倍。  
• 保持观望：Supabase支持者对这一变化感到意外，期待观察后续发展。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于项目控制权或商业归属变化能否带来更多资源，同时是否会牺牲兼容性、稳定性、性能及现有客户体验。

Blog
/
company
Supabase is acquiring Turso
2 Oct 2026
·
3 minute read
Paul Copplestone
CEO and Co-Founder
AI is enabling builders to create an immense amount of software. Today, agents are spinning up millions of databases to power the prototypes, explorations, dashboards, and apps they're building. This new pattern, at this massive scale, requires an evolution in database infrastructure. Turso is joining Supabase to build this evolution.
For existing users, nothing changes. Supabase will continue building around Postgres, while Turso will continue its work on SQLite. And together, we’re creating something new that will bring the Supabase experience to every agent.
Databases for agents
#
Supabase is already launching over one million databases per week. As agents build more software, we believe database demand will outpace the world’s current capacity to support them. So we need infrastructure that can scale to meet this growth and is suited to how we build with agents.
Agents should be able to create a database as easily as creating a file, with just as little concern about cost. For smaller workloads, that shouldn’t require provisioning a dedicated machine every time. Databases should be cheap to create, available on demand, and have a clear path to production when needed.
SQLite is well suited to these small, on-demand workloads. Postgres is what you want as your application scales. We want builders to have the same developer experience from prototyping to production.
Turso
#
Turso has built an architecture for exactly this pattern. They rebuilt SQLite in Rust and created a cloud platform where a single server can manage millions of databases, loading them when needed and suspending them when they’re not.
This architecture makes it possible to provision a database for each agent on demand, whether on Turso Cloud or in customers’ own clouds, as Superhuman, Sauna.ai, CTO.new, and Mastra do.
We share a vision for how infrastructure needs to evolve to support agentic AI. Turso will continue operating, with a clear path into the broader Supabase ecosystem as workloads grow.
Open source
#
Turso and Supabase have a lot in common: a commitment to open source, a focus on developer experience, and an appetite to tackle hard infrastructure problems.
We’re excited to welcome Glauber Costa and Pekka Enberg to Supabase with the rest of the Turso team. Glauber will lead this agentic infrastructure effort.
Our mission is to store the world’s data, and agents are going to create a lot more of it. This gets us closer to that goal.

data.title: Big Tech ruined the cloud, so we're renaming ours
data.author: 2sf5
data.article_summary: Nabu Casa将“Home Assistant Cloud”更名为“Home Assistant Link”，以准确体现其定位：为本地运行的Home Assistant提供可选的远程访问等服务，而非依赖云端运行。Link不锁定用户，取消订阅后智能家居仍可正常工作；用户数据加密且归用户所有，不用于变现。订阅收入大部分用于支持开放家庭基金会，推动项目长期发展、隐私保护与用户选择权。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Home Assistant 将“Cloud”更名为“Link”是否恰当，以及其背后的服务模式、隐私安全与品牌定位。

不同观点：
• 支持改名者认为，“Cloud”已被AWS、Google等大厂塑造成特定商业和隐私形象；“Link”更能体现连接用户与设备的功能，也可减少“依赖云端”的误解。有人因此开始关注其隐私声明。  
• 反对者认为本质未变，仍是托管在远程服务器上的付费专有SaaS，改名只是品牌包装；“Link”反而无法说明服务部署位置和收费性质。  
• 中立或淡化者指出，云计算本来就是付费托管服务，并未被“大科技”毁掉，改名主要是企业品牌选择；用户也可以不用，改用Tailscale、Cloudflare Tunnel、端口转发等方案。  
• 安全批评集中在权限和数据治理：缺少原生用户组、细粒度RBAC，难以限制儿童操作设备；有人因此改用MQTT。另有人要求先进行网络调用审计，担心分析数据、第三方SDK和隐私泄露。  
• 还有观点认为Home Assistant自身并非完全离线，安装和运行会访问Docker Hub及其他云服务，与其“离线优先、反云端”的宣传存在张力。

补充讨论：争议核心不是名称本身，而是“Link”能否真实反映其仍属云端SaaS，以及隐私、安全、权限控制是否足以支撑更积极的品牌定位。

49934228.article_content:
From ever-increasing subscription prices to outages and data harvesting: we don’t like what the cloud has come to represent. So we’re redefining what an online service should be: private, optional, and free from lock-in or walled gardens.
That’s why today Nabu Casa is renaming
Home Assistant Cloud
to more accurately describe what the service
actually does
, and to better reflect our values. Allow us to introduce:
Home Assistant Link
I’m Carl, Vice President of Commercial at Nabu Casa. You probably know us as the folks making all that sleek, highly optimized Home Assistant hardware. Beyond hardware, we also manage and run Home Assistant Link, and as one of the Open Home Foundation’s commercial partners, we’re here to help fund all their amazing work. We feel pretty passionately about the word cloud, and we’d love to explain how the old name never fit, and why Link finally does.
Created for the community
Home Assistant began with a group of core developers working nights and weekends alongside their regular jobs to create the platform – a good recipe for burnout, and one that has ended plenty of similar open source projects. So in 2018, we founded Nabu Casa and created Home Assistant Cloud to make sure that didn’t happen.
Home Assistant Cloud set out to make Home Assistant easier for more people to use, starting with a problem many of you had: reaching your Home Assistant when you’re not at home, without having to spend a weekend on it. It was also built to make Home Assistant’s development sustainable.
The intent was never to just ask for donations, but to build an optional service that benefited the community and funded the work at the same time. The majority of profits from subscriptions now fund the Open Home Foundation. That money supports everyone working on Home Assistant – from salaried staff to volunteers – keeping the project sustainable. That shift took Home Assistant from a passion project to one that could invest back into its community, and one that could stick around for the long haul.
A breath of fresh air
We even took it out of the Nabu Casa logo… did we take this too far?
🤔
We had a service that we and the community loved, but the name just didn’t feel right. For example, there were times when Paulus, founder of Home Assistant and President of the Open Home Foundation, was on stage saying “don’t buy products that require the cloud to work,” then in the next breath having to explain how Home Assistant Cloud is different, despite the name. That created unnecessary friction.
It also caused confusion, since some new users thought (and continue to think) Home Assistant Cloud is a way to run Home Assistant in the cloud. This has never been the case, because we believe Home Assistant should
always be run locally, in your home
.
Big Tech has given the cloud a bad name, and while Link does run online, it is very different from other cloud-powered smart home services:
Home Assistant Link
A Big Tech cloud
Optional:
your smart home will still work without it, lights and all.
Required:
all or most features won’t work without it.
No lock-in:
you can use this service or someone else’s, and you’ll never be stuck.
A walled garden:
you’ll be locked into that one service, and all its outages or price increases.
Your data’s private:
your data is yours, and will always stay that way.
Your data’s monetized:
you’re the product, and your data is used for ads, AI training, and sometimes sold to third parties.
Funds a nonprofit:
Nabu Casa contributes the majority of profits from subscriptions to the Open Home Foundation, supporting their fight for privacy, choice, and sustainability.
Funds investors first:
profits flow to shareholders, debt repayment, and a bunch of other stuff first, and funding developers is an afterthought.
Your subscriptions help sustain Home Assistant, but we’ve been clear from the beginning that you do not need Link to use the platform. We hate what Big Tech has done to smart devices, turning them into paperweights when they drop support. Thermostats that can’t be scheduled or cameras that can’t detect motion, giving the smart home a bad reputation and making a mountain of e-waste. By not using Link, you’ll miss out on some extras, but that’s all they are: extras. And if you
do
use Link but have to unsubscribe, your smart home will keep working.
Big Tech treats your data as a commodity and a tool for mass surveillance: sold to advertisers, used to train AI, and dealt to third parties for the best price. We think this is morally bankrupt. That’s why when you use Home Assistant Link, your data is encrypted, and only you have the key. Neither Nabu Casa nor the Open Home Foundation want your data, and we work hard to never have an opportunity to see it.
This is what tech serving people looks like: data that’s yours, and a smart home that answers to you – not corporate shareholders.
Choose your own path
Many of you build DIY projects to customize your setup, and Home Assistant isn’t going anywhere o

data.title: Mozilla shutting down Solo AI website creator
data.author: nedrylandJP
data.article_summary: Solo将于2026年11月30日关闭，届时所有网站、账户和数据将永久删除。用户应登录账户设置下载网站HTML、图片链接及表单数据，并在截止日前单独保存图片。Pro/Grow订阅未使用部分将按比例退款且不再续费。Solo购买的域名需迁移至Name.com。可考虑Wix、Squarespace、WordPress等替代服务，问题可联系support@soloist.ai。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Mozilla 关闭网站创建工具 Solo 的决定，评论集中质疑其项目取舍、AI 导向、资源管理及组织战略。

不同观点：
• **反对非核心项目、主张回归浏览器**：认为 AI 功能并未改善网络体验，Mozilla 应优先提升 Firefox、修复 Bugzilla 积压并推动 Web 标准，而不是开发用户未要求的工具。  
• **质疑 AI 热潮与项目价值**：多位评论者将 Solo 视为“AI 垃圾软件”或无谓副业，认为项目烧钱、分散了维护核心产品的资源；有人讽刺负责人可能靠 LLM 继续追逐下一个风口。  
• **批评管理和问责机制**：评论质疑谁应为此类投入负责、为何项目被砍却缺乏解释，并提到组织内部对平等议题的重视似乎下降。也有人要求提供关闭项目的具体理由和数据。  
• **对 Mozilla 整体战略失望**：有人认为 Mozilla 已失去相关性、长期无法有效商业化，并过度依赖 Google 资金；甚至认为其衰落客观上有利于 Google 压制竞争。另有人主张由 Canonical 等机构打造替代方案。  
• **相对中性的事实补充**：有用户分享自己曾用 Solo 建站，但特别说明网站评论为自动生成，暗示产品内容质量和实际价值有限。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 Solo 是否属于应及时削减的低价值试验，还是 Mozilla 探索收入来源、降低对 Google 依赖的必要尝试；评论总体明显偏负面。

49934502.article_content:
Solo Shutdown FAQ
We made the difficult decision to shut down Solo. Rest assured, we are here to help and to make the closure, and the migration of your existing site to another hosting provider, as seamless as possible.
How long do I have?
All Solo websites and data will be deleted on
November 30, 2026
. There will be no way to recover your site, account, or data after that date.
How do I download my website data?
Log in to
Solo
.
Click the menu at the top right, and select
Account Settings
.
In the Account Settings popup, click
Download Website Data
.
You'll receive a ZIP file containing an HTML export of your website and a CSV file with links to your image assets, as well as your contact form and newsletter submissions.
Image source files are not included in the ZIP.
Download each image individually from the links in the CSV file before the shutdown date on
November 30, 2026
.
What are some alternative hosting providers?
Wix
,
Squarespace
, and
WordPress
are popular website hosts. You can also consider AI website builders such as
Bolt
or
Lovable
.
What if I have a Solo Pro subscription?
If you have an active Solo Pro or Grow subscription, we will issue a prorated refund for the unused portion of your current billing period, calculated as of
October 1, 2026
. The refund goes back to your original payment method, and you don't need to do anything to receive it. Your subscription will not renew.
What if I purchased a Solo domain?
If you purchased a domain through Solo Domains (not IONOS), you will need to migrate it to
Name.com
, our domain partner. To do so:
Create a
Name.com account
. If you already have one, log in.
Verify the email address on your Name.com account. Name.com requires a verified account before it can accept the transfer. See Name.com's guide to
account and domain verification
.
Locate your unique
Account Code
, displayed in the top-right corner of the Name.com dashboard.
Email the Account Code to
support@soloist.ai
. We will transfer your Solo Domains account to Name.com and email you when it's complete.
Add your billing information to Name.com. If you don't, Name.com will remind you as your domain renewal date approaches.
Where can I get more assistance?
If you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to contact us at
support@soloist.ai
.

data.title: Giving friends custom text buzzes based on Morse code
data.author: evakhoury
data.article_summary: 作者因不想查看手机，便为约25位朋友设置了独特的短信震动，并以对方姓名首字母对应的摩斯密码设计震动节奏，从而仅凭口袋中的震动判断发信人。作者手动在 iPhone 设置中录制并分配震动，借助 Claude 制作的摩斯密码节拍工具提高效率，整个过程约45分钟。作者还提醒：紧急联系应打电话，因为短信可能无法及时看到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：诺基亚经典提示音与摩尔斯电码的巧妙设计，以及能否将类似机制用于现代手机的铃声、通知和触觉反馈。

不同观点：
• [aorist]指出，诺基亚默认短信提示音实际对应摩尔斯电码“S-M-S”，“Ascending”铃声则拼出“CONNECTING PEOPLE”，强调其隐藏含义与品牌创意。  
• [ragmondo]分享过往开发经验：曾开发允许来电者为对方设备设置铃声的 Android 应用，但 iOS 因权限和系统限制难以实现；认为此类功能目前仍更适合 Android，并提到相关专利风险较低、已有先例。  
• [taylor-tg]认为把文字转换成摩尔斯电码很聪明，也能帮助用户被动学习摩尔斯码；提出 iOS 可将音频提示与触觉同步，或通过生成音频文件、分享菜单、Shortcuts/Automator 实现自动化。  
• [tjoff]设想让手机用震动直接传递短信内容，但指出现有震动马达太弱，难以辨认；建议增加独立蜂鸣器，或通过特定触摸动作获取更详细的信息。

补充讨论：争议主要不在创意本身，而在平台能力、用户授权与硬件限制：iOS 的系统权限不如 Android 灵活，触觉设备也可能无法清晰表达复杂信息。

49925653.article_content:
liquidbrain
Giving friends custom text buzzes based on morse code
Published on
September 30, 2026
I ran out of time to write a good blog post
for September
, so I wrote a quick blog post for September. Oops!
I sometimes have my phone in my pocket with notifications on. When that happens, I can feel every time my phone buzzes. I know when someone has texted me because I have a custom vibration pattern for text messages that is distinct from other notifications. However, I have historically had few distinctions between different people, so I don't know
who
has texted me.
I find this annoying. Of all the notifications on my phone, texts have the highest signal-to-noise ratio. Most texts I receive are individual messages from friends or colleagues. However, at any given time, there's maybe only a 40% chance that a text is actually relevant to what I'm currently doing.
So either I bring my phone out of my pocket, or I get curious wondering who has texted me. (I particularly enjoy getting texts out of the blue, so it's a distracting thought.)
While I generally keep my notifications off to avoid this problem, there are times when I am expecting a text response from someone that I need to respond to quickly.
1
In such cases, I'd like a way to know when the text is actually relevant.
With an iPhone, it's possible to give custom text buzzes to different people. In the past, I've done this for my family members. But I've wanted a way to distinguish more people in my life.
Recently, I got fed up and made custom text tones for about 25 people I know. Because I wanted to be systematic, I gave each person text tones based on the Morse Code of their initials.
How I did it
I wish I could have done this in an automated manner, but I ended up having to make each text tone by hand. The whole process took about 45 minutes.
I figured out which friends I wanted to start with and recorded the buzz pattern for each individually. I did all the recording from the centralized place in Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Text Tone > Haptics > Create New Vibration. (It's possible to record a new vibration directly from a contact, but that's more annoying because you can't switch apps midway through). I then named the text tone the initials of the person in question.
Then, to update a individual contact, I opened each contact, clicked Edit > Text Tone > Haptics, and then clicked the already-made vibration pattern.
One thing made recording the vibrations a lot easier. I had Claude make me an artifact where I could press on someone's initials and the Morse Code pattern would play as a series of beats. Here's what it
looked like
.
